explanation: The statement is the tower-coherence of the file's own map `extensionMap k L K R = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom L L K) (AlgHom.id k R)`: it says the two one-step tensor-product maps L⊗R → M⊗R → K⊗R compose to the one-step map L⊗R → K⊗R. I searched Mathlib for a matching declaration: `Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp` (RingTheory/TensorProduct/Maps.lean:551) and `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.map_comp` (LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Tower.lean:197), `TensorProduct.map_comp`/`map_map` (LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Map.lean:104,108), plus `Algebra.TensorProduct.map_*` (`map_id`, `map_id_comp`, `map_comp_id`, `map_comp_includeLeft/Right`, `comm_comp_map`, `congr_trans`, `cancelBaseChange*`, `baseChange_baseChange`) and `IsScalarTower`/`AlgHom` lemmas (`IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq`, `algebraMap_apply`, `AlgHom.comp_algebraMap_of_tower`, `AlgHom.restrictScalars`) in Algebra/Algebra/Tower.lean. None states the tower case: every `map_comp`-type lemma in Mathlib composes two tensor-product maps whose first components are homomorphisms over one and the same base ring S, whereas here the two steps live over L and over M respectively (the second needs `AlgHom.restrictScalars L`), and the composite first component `((toAlgHom M M K).restrictScalars L).comp (toAlgHom L L M)` must first be identified with `toAlgHom L L K` via `AlgHom.ext` and `IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply L M K`. That identification (an auxiliary AlgHom/`algebraMap`-composition fact, not merely an instantiation of the lemma's arguments) is required in any derivation from `map_comp`, so the result is not obtainable in one or two lines of routine glue from any single Mathlib declaration; the library's own proof does a tensor induction instead and uses no such Mathlib statement (`proof_uses_it` = false). Hence no duplicate and no (two-line) special case was found.
